h: Where it is and what's around it
p: The Flower Bowl is at Barton, on the northern side of Preston along the A6, so it's easy to reach by car from the city, the M6 and the towns further north towards Garstang and Lancaster. Being on the edge of the countryside, it feels a bit more relaxed than a city-centre leisure complex.

It's a real all-weather option. With bowling, curling, crazy golf and a cinema all under one roof, you can fill a whole rainy day without stepping back outside, which makes it a popular choice in school holidays. Booking ahead is the safest way to secure your preferred times, especially for curling, which tends to run in set sessions.

If you're new to curling, don't worry. It's one of those activities that looks gentle but quickly turns competitive. Wear comfortable, flat shoes with a decent grip, wrap up warm because you'll be on real ice, and be ready for plenty of laughs as the sweepers try to steer the stone.

Out in the fresh air, Beacon Fell Country Park is a short drive away, with woodland trails and views over the Fylde coast and towards the Lake District hills on a clear day. It's a lovely contrast to an indoor day.

In Preston itself, Avenham and Miller Parks run down to the River Ribble and are perfect for a stroll and a picnic. The market town of Garstang, to the north, is also worth a wander for its independent shops and canal-side walks.
